newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN GOVT MULLS MUNICIPAL BOND MARKET.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN GOVT MULLS MUNICIPAL BOND MARKET.

text.p: The government was considering an active municipal bond market to help finance local authorities, finance department director-general Maria Ramos said on Tuesday.
But she told the parliamentary finance committee that a great deal of work had to be done first to ensure stability and sustainability in the way municipal finances were managed.
"What is happening at local government level is important to the financial well-being of the country," she said.
Her department was actively involved in trying to help municipalities improve their financial management and had become much stricter about rejecting budgets that were out of line.
"Ultimately we see one of our roles as being the maintenance of a sustainable financial position within the country," she said.
In the longer term, her department had started discussing the possibility of municipal bonds with financial institutions.
Chief director in charge of assets and liabilities Koen Kruger told the committee that one financial institution had already started setting up a ratings system for local authorities.
